Subject: Trial deployment options & success gates — TrustMed

Hi Elaine / TrustMed team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — really useful to understand your evaluation priorities. I wanted to capture a concise post-call recap + my recommended path for the 4-week trial and immediate next steps so we all have alignment.

Summary of requirements we heard:
- Data: PHI adjacency but no direct patient identifiers in initial eval; encryption at rest + audit logs required.
- Performance: interactive search latency target ~ p50 < 120ms, p95 < 300ms.
- Throughput: expected peak ~ 40 QPS for ranking + 10 concurrent embedding jobs.
- Evaluation metrics: retrieval R@10, end-to-end latency, cost-per-1k-tokens, and regression-free answers on your 150 core prompts.

Deployment options (tradeoffs) — brief:
1) Hosted Redwood API (fastest onboarding) — pros: <1 day setup, streaming, auto-scaling; cons: less network isolation, data flows through our managed service.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved GPU pool) — pros: predictable throughput, isolated tenancy, easier performance testing; cons: ~3–5 day setup for reservation & tuning.
3) Private VPC (customer-managed VPC peering) — pros: full network isolation, best for regulated data; cons: longer setup (2–3 weeks) and procurement.

Our recommended phased approach:
- Week 0 (smoke): Hosted Redwood API — quick sanity checks using a sanitized subset of your prompts and sample embeddings.
- Week 1–2 (load & perf): Dedicated sandbox provisioned for peak-run tests (batch embeddings + 40 QPS spike tests).
- Week 3–4 (final validation): If you need network isolation or KMS/HSM, move to Private VPC for compliance sign-off; otherwise continue on Dedicated and validate SLA objectives.

Success gates (must-pass to consider trial successful):
- KPI 1: Retrieval R@10 >= 0.68 on the 150 prompt set.
- KPI 2: p95 latency <= 300ms for interactive flows under T1 load profile (40 QPS).
- KPI 3: Cost: sustained inference cost <= $0.65 per 1k tokens (projected).
- KPI 4: Audit logs + encryption-at-rest confirmed and accessible to your auditors.

Ownership & who-does-what:
- Lauren (me): overall trial coordination + commercial touchpoint; procurement liaison.
- Marcus (eng): technical lead — environment provisioning, load scripts, and kernel/quantization recommendations.
- Monica (CS): onboarding, success criteria validation, and prompt-set management.
- Elaine (TrustMed): product lead — provide sample prompt set, any representative data, and procurement contact.

Attachments: I attached a lightweight trial-checklist and an architecture PDF that outlines the VPC flow.

Next immediate asks (by EOD Fri):
1) Elaine — confirm whether TrustMed will require VPC/KMS for the pilot or if hosted is acceptable for the first-week smoke test.
2) Elaine — share redacted sample prompt set (<= 150 prompts) + one representative corpus file for embedding tests.
3) Lauren/Marcus/Monica — we will prepare a Dedicated sandbox quote and a 1-week hosted access token.

If that sounds good I’ll file the HubSpot playbook and propose kickoff for Monday (3/20).

Best,

Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Trial deployment options & success gates — TrustMed

Hi Lauren — thanks for the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) For Week 0 smoke we are OK starting on Hosted provided we (a) keep all PII/PHI out of the sample dataset and (b) can export audit logs for the smoke session. Procurement will still need a short MSA addendum but that shouldn’t block the smoke test.
2) VPC: we do expect to require VPC + customer-managed KMS if the trial progresses to anything that touches live data. For the initial eval (sanitized data) hosted is acceptable.
3) KPIs: R@10 >= 0.68 looks reasonable; for latency p95 we’d prefer <= 250ms if possible. If that’s tight, please call out the expected delta for embedding/reranking flows.

We can provide the 150 prompt set by Friday EOD and a representative CSV (anonymized). Procurement looped in — procurement@trustmed.com will coordinate contract paperwork.

Elaine
Elaine Wu
Senior Product Manager, TrustMed
elaine.wu@trustmed.com
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trial deployment options & success gates — TrustMed

Thanks — quick tech notes from my side:

- Hosted: We can enable streaming + prefix caching right away. Audit logs: we can export request/response IDs and redact payloads for the smoke test.
- Dedicated sandbox: I estimate 3 business days to spin up a reserved pool and run our baseline perf tuning (quantization profile, kernel selection). We’ll need a small sample of your corpus to create representative max-seq and embedding size distributions.
- VPC: typical setup with VPC peering + customer KMS takes ~10 business days because of routing and cert exchange; we can parallelize some items.

On KPIs: the difference between p95=250ms and p95=300ms often depends on batching strategy for the retrieval+rerank step. If you’re targeting 250ms we’ll prioritize a Dedicated sandbox and tune batch sizes and KV-cache eviction. I’ll sketch a short test-plan:
  * Baseline: hosted, 1k prompt run (sanitized) — measure p50/p95.
  * Spike: Dedicated sandbox — run T1 load profile (40 QPS) with concurrency matrix and measure p95 + CPU/GPU utilization.
  * Final: If VPC requested, validate identical perf once peered.

Action items for me: provision load harness, share expected flag toggles for batch size and quantization; need sample CSV by Fri to proceed.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
